outcome: admission to a neonatal care unit
cohort: The study included 13,136 pregnant women from 12 studies across 12 countries, comparing those with SARS-CoV-2 infection to confirmed negative pregnancies, along with their neonates.
finding: SARS-CoV-2 infection at any time during pregnancy significantly increases the risk of maternal death, severe maternal morbidities, and neonatal morbidity, but not stillbirth or intrauterine growth restriction.
